notes.non_compete: Non-compete clauses during employment are void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act 1872. Post-termination non-competes are generally unenforceable in India.
notes.liquidated_damages: Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, courts may award only 'reasonable compensation' even if liquidated damages are stipulated.
notes.indemnification: Indemnification is governed by Sections 124-147. Only losses caused by the indemnifier's act (or breach) are recoverable.
notes.data_privacy: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP) 2023 requires consent for data processing, data localization for certain categories, and breach notification within 72 hours.
notes.arbitration: Arbitration Act 1996 (amended 2019) governs. Indian courts have limited power to intervene in arbitral proceedings.
notes.stamp_duty: Agreements may require stamping under the Indian Stamp Act; unstamped agreements may not be admissible as evidence.
notes.governing_law: Indian courts generally respect choice-of-law clauses, but public policy exceptions apply.

notes.non_compete: Non-compete agreements are generally VOID in California under B&P Code §16600. Exceptions are extremely narrow (sale of business).
notes.data_privacy: CCPA/CPRA provides consumers with rights to know, delete, and opt-out of sale of personal data. Businesses must comply if they meet thresholds.
notes.at_will_employment: California is an at-will employment state, but wrongful termination exceptions apply.
notes.indemnification: Indemnity clauses are generally enforceable but subject to reasonableness standards.
notes.non_solicit: Employee non-solicitation clauses are also generally unenforceable in California.
notes.governing_law: California law may be applied regardless of choice-of-law clause if the employee primarily works in California.

notes.non_compete: Non-competes are enforceable if reasonable in scope, time, and geography. Courts apply a reasonableness test.
notes.governing_law: Delaware is the preferred jurisdiction for corporate contracts due to well-developed business law.
notes.liability: Delaware courts generally enforce limitation of liability clauses in commercial contracts.
notes.indemnification: Delaware permits broad indemnification provisions, including for officers and directors.

notes.non_compete: Non-competes are enforceable if they protect legitimate business interests and are reasonable in time, geography, and scope. Recent legislative efforts aim to ban them.
notes.data_privacy: SHIELD Act requires reasonable safeguards for private information of NY residents.
notes.liquidated_damages: NY courts enforce liquidated damages if they are a reasonable estimate of actual damages and not a penalty.
notes.governing_law: NY law is commonly chosen for commercial contracts. §5-1401 permits parties to choose NY law for contracts over $250K.

notes.non_compete: Restrictive covenants are enforceable only if they protect a legitimate business interest and are no wider than reasonably necessary.
notes.liability: Under UCTA 1977, exclusion of liability for death/personal injury caused by negligence is void. Other exclusions must be reasonable.
notes.data_privacy: UK GDPR requires lawful basis for processing, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, and 72-hour breach notification.
notes.unfair_terms: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 may render unfair terms in consumer contracts unenforceable.
notes.indemnification: Indemnity clauses are subject to the reasonableness test under UCTA for B2B contracts.

notes.non_compete: Rules vary by member state. Generally must be limited in time (typically 1-2 years) and compensated in some jurisdictions (e.g., France, Germany).
notes.data_privacy: GDPR requires explicit consent or legitimate interest for data processing, right to erasure, data portability, DPO appointment for certain controllers, and 72-hour breach notification to supervisory authority.
notes.unfair_terms: Directive 93/13/EEC renders unfair terms in consumer contracts not individually negotiated as non-binding.
notes.liability: Limitation of liability for personal injury or death is generally unenforceable across EU member states.
notes.governing_law: Rome I Regulation governs choice of law for contractual obligations. Consumer protection laws of the consumer's habitual residence cannot be derogated.
